summary_paragraph: A 68-year-old male with a history of tracheostomy, atrial fibrillation, diabetes, and chronic urinary retention was admitted from a nursing home for altered mental status and fever. He was found to be in septic shock with a Proteus bacteremia likely originating from a urinary tract infection, evidenced by 2.5 liters of purulent urine upon Foley catheter exchange. He was treated with fluid resuscitation, vasopressors, and broad-spectrum antibiotics, later narrowed to meropenem based on culture sensitivities. His acute kidney injury and hypernatremia resolved with treatment. A PICC line was placed to complete a 14-day antibiotic course outpatient. His atrial fibrillation was managed with bridging anticoagulation, and he was discharged to extended care in stable condition.
